translation:
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ hrīḥ
In the palace of magnetizing power, the blazing of great bliss,
The wisdom body of discerning the union of bliss and emptiness,
From the nature of the lotus of unattached bliss,
The glorious splendor of the great illuminating vajra sun.

translation:
Dharmakāya Amitābha and Vajradharma,
Avalokiteśvara, the form of compassion’s passion,
Padma Gyalpo, who holds dominion over all of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa,
Powerful Heruka, Subjugator of All Appearance and Existence.

translation:
Assembly of magnetizing vajra heroes and ḍākinīs,
Within the very state of the great equality of appearance and emptiness,
You cause the three realms of existence to tremble with the dance of your vajra body,
You summon the three worlds with the laughter of your unceasing speech.

translation:
And pervade the whole of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa with rays of red light,
You cause the refined essence of cyclic existence and peace to vibrate and be gathered in,
Through your enlightened mind of great vajra passion,
You grant the supreme of all desired things—the two kinds of accomplishments.

translation:
With your great vajra hook and lasso,
You bind all appearance and existence within great bliss,
Possessing the dance of the infinite net of magical illusion,
Residing as densely as a split-open pod of sesame seeds.

translation:
To the infinite hosts of magnetizing deities of the Three Roots,
I pray with devotion: grant your blessings!
Grant the accomplishment of unobstructed mastery,
Over all the glorious, desired attainments, both supreme and ordinary.

translation: This was composed by one bearing the name Dhī on the first day of the seventh month of the Earth-Hare year. It is certain that whoever prays in this way will accomplish all magnetizing activities exactly as they have intended. It will also be accomplished by writing this on a red silk banner and hoisting it, or by using it in a fire or wind prayer wheel. Maṅgalam.
